name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_CH07_MCQ_Q01 - Cells forming inner walls of blood vessels

questiontext.text: Which one of the following types of cell is involved in making of the inner walls of blood vessels?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Epithelial tissues form the covering or lining of external and internal body surfaces. Simple epithelium consists of a single layer of cells and functions as a lining for body cavities, ducts, and tubes.

Step 2: Evaluation
Simple squamous epithelium is composed of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries. Because of its thin structure, it forms an effective diffusion boundary and lines the inner walls of blood vessels (endothelium) and air sacs of lungs. Cuboidal epithelium is mainly found in ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons, columnar epithelium lines the stomach and intestine, and stratified epithelium provides protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Squamous epithelium is involved in forming the inner walls of blood vessels.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_CH07_MCQ_Q02 - Category of tissue for adipose tissue

questiontext.text: To which one of the following categories does adipose tissue belong?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animal tissues are broadly classified into four types: epithelial, connective, muscular, and neural tissues.

Step 2: Evaluation
Connective tissues are the most abundant and widely distributed tissues in complex animals, serving to link and support other tissues or organs. Adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin, whose cells are specialised to store fats.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Adipose tissue belongs to the connective tissue category.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_CH07_MCQ_Q03 - Identifying tissue that is not connective

questiontext.text: Which one of the following is not a connective tissue?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Connective tissues include loose connective tissue, dense connective tissue, and specialised connective tissues such as cartilage, bones, and blood.

Step 2: Evaluation
Bone and cartilage are supportive specialised connective tissues, while blood is a fluid specialised connective tissue containing plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Muscles, however, constitute muscular tissue, which is specialised for contraction and movement.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Muscles are not a connective tissue.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_CH07_MCQ_Q04 - Segments bearing setae in earthworm

questiontext.text: Setae help in locomotion in earthworm but are not uniformly present in all the segments. They are present in

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In earthworms, locomotion is aided by rows of S-shaped chitinous structures called setae, which are embedded in epidermal pits in the middle of body segments.

Step 2: Evaluation
Setae are present in every body segment of the earthworm except the first segment (peristomium), the last segment (anal segment), and the clitellar segments (segments 14 to 16). Therefore, segments 20 to 22 bear setae.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Setae are present in the 20th - 22nd segment.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_CH07_MCQ_Q05 - True anatomical statement for cockroach

questiontext.text: Which one of the following statements is true for cockroach?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cockroaches (Periplaneta americana) exhibit sexual dimorphism and undergo paurometabolous development.

Step 2: Evaluation
Male cockroaches bear a pair of short, thread-like anal styles on the 9th sternum, which are absent in females. Regarding the other biological facts: each ovary in a female cockroach is formed of a group of eight (not ten) ovarian tubules or ovarioles; development occurs through nymphal stages (not a caterpillar larva); and cockroaches are uricotelic (excreting uric acid), not ureotelic.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The true statement for cockroach is that anal styles are absent in females.

answer.text: The number of ovarioles in each ovary are ten.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_CH07_MATCHING_Q06 - Matching animal tissues with locations and functions

questiontext.text: Match the following and choose the correct option.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different animal tissues have specialised structures suited to their specific locations and physiological roles.

Step 2: Evaluation
Adipose tissue is a loose connective tissue specialised for fat storage beneath the skin. Stratified epithelium consists of multiple cell layers providing protection, as found in the skin. Hyaline cartilage is a pliable skeletal connective tissue present in the tip of the nose. Blood is a fluid connective tissue that circulates substances throughout the body.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairs are: Adipose tissue with Fat storage; Stratified epithelium with Skin; Hyaline cartilage with Nose; and Fluid connective tissue with Blood.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_CH07_MATCHING_Q07 - Matching earthworm biological terms and descriptions

questiontext.text: Match the following and choose the correct option.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Earthworms exhibit specific reproductive, developmental, sensory, and circulatory features characteristic of annelids.

Step 2: Evaluation
A hermaphrodite (bisexual) organism possesses both testis and ovary in the same animal. Direct development refers to development in which a larval form is absent and young ones resemble adults. Chemoreceptors are sensory structures that detect chemical substances. In earthworms, blood glands present in the 4th, 5th, and 6th segments produce blood cells and haemoglobin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairs are: Hermaphrodite with Testis and ovary in the same animal; Direct development with Larval form absent; Chemoreceptor with Sense of chemical substances; and Blood gland in earthworm with Produces blood cells and haemoglobin.

answer.text: Testis and ovary in the same animal

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_CH07_MATCHING_Q08 - Matching cockroach reproductive structures and roles

questiontext.text: Match the following with reference to cockroach and choose the correct option.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The male and female reproductive systems of a cockroach contain specialised anatomical structures for gamete formation and transfer.

Step 2: Evaluation
Phallomeres (male gonapophyses) are asymmetrical chitinous structures representing the external genitalia of the male cockroach. The male gonopore is the opening of the ejaculatory duct situated ventral to the anus. Sperms are glued together in the seminal vesicles to form bundles of sperm called spermatophores. In females, each ovary consists of eight ovarioles, each containing a chain of developing ova.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairs are: Phallomere with The external genitalia; Gonopore with Opening of the ejaculatory duct; Spermatophore with Bundles of sperm; and Ovarioles with Chain of developing ova.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_CH07_MATCHING_Q09 - Matching frog sensory and neural structures

questiontext.text: Match the following and choose the correct option.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The nervous system and sense organs of a frog coordinate sensory perception and neural transmission.

Step 2: Evaluation
In frogs, the organs of touch are sensory papillae, and the organ of smell is the nasal epithelium. Cranial nerves (10 pairs in frogs) arise from the brain and form part of the peripheral nervous system. The medulla oblongata passes out through the foramen magnum and continues into the spinal cord enclosed in the vertebral column.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairs are: Touch with Sensory papillae; Smell with Nasal epithelium; Cranial nerves with Peripheral nervous system; and Medulla oblongata with Foramen magnum.
